title: What AWS's chief AI and technology officer told employees about the future of AI
summary: At the AWS Global Meeting, Matt Wood drew a parallel between AI today and cloud's early days—and brought a live demo to prove the future is already here.
body_markdown:
---


## Key takeaways


- AWS is building the foundational tools for AI the same way it built them for cloud computing.


- Odyssey unveiled Agora-2, an AI that simulates shared worlds with no game engine.


- From world models to code synthesis, frontier startups are building on AWS Trainium.


---


At the AWS Global Meeting on September 17, AWS Chief AI and Technology Officer Matt Wood laid out a vision for where AI is heading—and brought a live demo on stage to prove it’s already arriving.


“What we are doing today at AWS for AI is exactly what we did for cloud computing, to make this technology broadly distributed and democratized for everybody,” Wood told the audience.


Then he named the building blocks:


[Trainium](https://www.aboutamazon.com/stories/ai-chips-aws-Trainium2-explain) for compute,


[Bedrock](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/aws/aws-ceo-ai-inference-transforms-developer-capabilities) for inference,


[AgentCore](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/aws/aws-amazon-bedrock-agent-core-ai-agents) for agents—and brought the startups already building on them to prove it.


[How the next generation of AI researchers is using Amazon chips to accelerate discovery](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/aws/amazon-trainium-investment-university-ai-research)


University researchers are using Amazon’s Trainium chip to push the boundaries of their work—and making the chip better for all developers in the process.


## A startup demonstrates its most realistic world simulator yet


The centerpiece of the meeting was a live demonstration from Odyssey, a startup building foundation world models—a new kind of AI that learns physics by watching massive amounts of video rather than relying on hand-coded rules.


“A language model learns to predict the next most likely word in a sentence. A world model learns to predict the next most likely future of a world,” explained Oliver Cameron, CEO of Odyssey.


World models learn how the world works—from physics and cause-and-effect to human behavior—providing a foundational intelligence that can be applied across many industries. A world model draws on extensive learned knowledge of the world to automate physical systems, train AIs in interactive environments, and much more across robotics, autonomous driving, science, healthcare, education, gaming, defense, energy, and beyond.


[AWS commits more than $500 million to student cloud and AI training](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/aws/aws-student-rewards-free-cloud-ai-training)


Through a new Student Rewards program on AWS Builder Center, university students worldwide can earn credits, premium training, and certification vouchers.


On stage Cameron introduced


[Odyssey-3](https://odyssey.systems/introducing-odyssey-3) , Odyssey's most advanced foundation world model yet, which is trained and runs on Trainium3. Odyssey-3 is trained on vast observations of the world, giving it a learned grasp of physics, cause-and-effect, and human behavior. The same model can control robots, power humanoids, drive vehicles, pilot drones, train other AIs, and play video games. Because Odyssey-3 already understands how the world works, it can learn new tasks quickly, with far less task-specific data than previous systems.


Additionally, Cameron unveiled Agora-2, a multi-agent world model—the first to hold multiple intelligences inside the same simulated world at the same time. Cameron and Wood each picked up controllers and entered Agora-2 in real time. The audience watched on a split screen as both navigated, interacted, and fought within the same AI-generated environment, each from their own perspective. Agora-2 supports up to 20 participants in a single simulation, with no game engine underneath.


Cameron, who spent a decade working on autonomous vehicles before founding Odyssey, said the implications go well beyond gaming. “I believe we are on the cusp of a GPT-3 moment for world models,” he said. “This is the moment where we see an explosion of applications for world models, and their adoption into every industry imaginable.”


## OpenClaw creator Peter Steinberger on AI's next chapter


The meeting also featured a fireside chat between Peter Steinberger, the creator of


[OpenClaw](https://openclaws.io/) and now at OpenAI, and AWS Vice President Francesca Vasquez. Steinberger discussed how the tools and infrastructure available to AI developers are evolving, a conversation that underscored Wood's broader argument that the biggest names in AI are building on and alongside AWS.


Steinberger has become one of open source's biggest recent success stories. His OpenClaw project, which Vasquez called "the fastest growing open source project in GitHub history," has drawn more than 388,000 GitHub stars and 3.2 million active users. The bigger shift, he argued, is in how software itself gets built. "It's no longer 'I write code.' It's more, how can I design a system so my agent can do its best work?" As he put it, "We're all moving a little bit up the ladder. We're not just coders anymore."


[Millions of students can now get access to a free year of Kiro from AWS](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/aws/amazon-expands-free-kiro-access-students-universities)


AWS is giving students at 132 universities across 18 countries a full year of free access to Kiro, so they enter the workforce ready to build with AI from day one.


## Why frontier AI startups are choosing AWS Trainium


A common thread across the meeting was the role of


[AWS Trainium](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/aws/amazon-ai-chips-business-history) in powering frontier AI workloads that demand sustained compute over weeks—a profile that general-purpose hardware struggles to sustain. Odyssey-3 runs on Trainium3 at over 80% model flops utilization—roughly double the industry average, according to the company.


Odyssey joins a


[growing network of startups building on Trainium](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/aws/why-ai-startups-choose-amazon-trainium-chips) , including DeCart AI (real-time game environments), Neura Robotics (physical AI), Reactor (world model infrastructure), Splash Music (music generation), and Poolside (code synthesis).


“


We're here because you moved fast when we needed it, and then built something really special with us,” Cameron said of AWS.


Wood closed with a vision for where all of it is heading. "Our goal at AWS is to make it as easy, cheap, and fast to build these valuable economically viable AI systems as it is for anyone to build a website today," he said. "It's happening now, it's happening fast, and it's happening in all industries, but most importantly of all, it's happening here on AWS."
